clue.text: Note small pig's appropriate noise

parts.note: G is a musical note, one of the letters A to G of the scale
a runt is the smallest, weakest piglet of a litter

explanation.surface: A remark that a grunt is just the sound for a little pig to make.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the rest of the clue: the noise appropriate to a pig, small or not.
explanation.definitionFit: A grunt is the low snorting sound typical of pigs, so it is their fitting noise.

clue.text: Group governing in cunning move to curtail debate

indicators.note: in places the group-and-governing pieces inside the word for cunning

parts.note: a lot is a group or batch

explanation.surface: A clique in power makes a crafty manoeuvre to cut a debate short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' seems part of 'cunning move' but belongs to the definition. A guillotine in Parliament is a motion limiting debate time.
explanation.definitionFit: In Parliament, a guillotine is a timetable motion that cuts discussion short to force a vote.

clue.text: Uniformed leader required on navy vessel

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An officer in uniform is needed aboard a naval ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container; 'required on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Fish is almost too dry when served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means read upwards, in reverse
almost means the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A fish dish is a little overcooked when it reaches the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims TOO to TO; 'when served up' reverses TO + BRUT to make the fish. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbot is a large flatfish prized as food.

clue.text: School spirit, half lazy and overr sentimental

annotationWithheld.why: School spirit, half lazy and overr sentimental: the scan prints 'over-sentimental' (definition; SCH + MALT + ZY), but the held clue's asPrinted marks 'overr' as the print's spelling, so the apply refuses the scan correction
annotationWithheld.clue: School spirit, half lazy and overr sentimental

clue.text: That woman going to call keeps one very obviously excited

indicators.note: keeps means holds the other pieces inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to ring is to call on the phone

explanation.surface: A woman about to phone someone is plainly worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' puts IV inside SHE, then RING follows; 'going to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shivering is trembling, the visible quivering of someone thrilled or agitated.

clue.text: Who might have got about year to finish off Creation?

definitions.text: Who might have got about year to finish off Creation?

indicators.note: about means surrounding the year abbreviation
the finish of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Which composer may have taken around a year to complete The Creation?
explanation.walkthrough: Haydn composed the oratorio The Creation; the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn wrote the oratorio The Creation, so he is the one who finished it.

clue.text: Broadcast snooker game, a large part from Lancaster

parts.note: a frame is a single game in a snooker match

explanation.surface: Televising a snooker match, with much of it coming from Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster is not the city but the Avro Lancaster, a WWII British bomber.
explanation.definitionFit: The airframe is the body of an aircraft, a big component of a Lancaster bomber.

clue.text: Country's cry of derision for America's position of war fighting superiority

definitions.text: America's position of war fighting superiority

parts.note: Turkey is a country; with 's it supplies the S

explanation.surface: A nation jeers at the USA's military dominance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link. A turkey shoot is American slang for a one-sided battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey shoot is US slang for a fight in which one side is overwhelmingly dominant.

clue.text: Shout like a coward giving out cry of pain

indicators.note: giving out means letting go of, dropping the cry from the word

parts.note: ow is a cry of pain

explanation.surface: A coward's shout is a yelp of pain.
explanation.definitionFit: A yell is a loud shout or cry.

clue.text: In run-down area, pub's prosperity halved, as clubs move in

indicators.note: the clubs symbol is put inside what remains of the halved word
only the back half of the word prosperity is kept, its first five letters dropped

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A pub in a poor district has lost half its takings as gangs arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' leaves ERITY, the back half of PROSPERITY; 'move in' puts C inside it to make ERCITY. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner city is the older central district, often associated with deprivation and neglect.

clue.text: In the country of two rivers

parts.note: R abbreviates river; the Ural is a river flowing between Europe and Asia
R abbreviates river; the Ural is a river flowing between Europe and Asia

explanation.surface: A land described by its two rivers.
explanation.walkthrough: One river is the abbreviation R, the other the Ural; 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes things in or of the countryside, away from towns.

clue.text: None see solver going wrong become suddenly afraid

indicators.note: the words are going wrong, so their letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A solver who sees nothing in a puzzle panics.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose your nerve is an idiom for suddenly lacking courage, turning fearful.

clue.text: Genius then runs out after set-ends as this puzzle is done

annotationWithheld.why: Genius then runs out after set-ends as this puzzle is done (5,6): GENIUS THEN gives ten of the eleven letters; 'set-ends' supplies S and T, one T too many, and no search or scan gives a sound parse
annotationWithheld.clue: Genius then runs out after set-ends as this puzzle is done

clue.text: Fight encountered over aluminium waste that's recyclable

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means placed above the next piece

parts.note: Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A fight broke out over aluminium rubbish that can be reused.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap metal is discarded metal collected for reprocessing.

clue.text: Travel on towards country

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another comes after it

explanation.surface: Moving on in the direction of some land.
explanation.definitionFit: Togo is a nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Torch song, perhaps, is a popular genre

parts.note: a song is an example of music, hence perhaps

explanation.surface: A torch song is said to be a well-liked style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Torch song' reads as one musical phrase, but torch and song work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Light music is a recognised easy-listening category of music with wide appeal.

clue.text: What might set off hard faces

definitions.text: What might set off hard faces

indicators.note: set off means rearranged, the letters set going in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Something to flatter tough features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set off' also means complement: a headscarf frames and softens a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A headscarf is worn around the head and can frame the face attractively.

clue.text: How glaze appears crazed over it with a lot of use

indicators.note: crazed suggests broken up, so the letters are mixed
a lot of the word use means most of it, dropping its last letter

explanation.surface: A glaze with fine cracks after heavy wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazed' is a pottery term for a glaze with fine cracks. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Vitreous means glassy, the look of a fired ceramic glaze.

clue.text: City reportedly getting tied up with inexpert player

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the phrase is said aloud and a word sounding the same is used

parts.note: a ham is a poor, overacting performer

explanation.surface: A city is said to be caught up with an incompetent performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nottingham is a city in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: The flower of Stratford's returning as star

indicators.note: returning tells us to read the river's name backwards

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; Stratford stands on the Avon

explanation.surface: The finest bloom of Shakespeare's town comes back as a celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' must be read as flow-er, a river: Stratford-upon-Avon is Shakespeare's town. 'as' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness.

clue.text: Poet wanting new and empty way by which to approach Little Gidding?

definitions.text: way by which to approach Little Gidding?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, the letter is removed
empty means the middle is removed, leaving first and last letters

explanation.surface: A poet goes without novelty on the way to a small village, as in Eliot's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Gidding is a tiny English hamlet, also the title of T. S. Eliot's poem; the question mark marks the small place as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A byroad is a minor side road, the kind that leads to a small village.

clue.text: Shy Sally finds everyone out to inhibit what's central to her functioning

indicators.note: out signals that the letters for everyone are taken away from the name

parts.note: to stem is to check or hold back

explanation.surface: A timid girl called Sally finds everybody away, which holds her back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes ALL from SALLY, leaving SY; 'finds' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The nervous system, brain and nerves, is the network at the core of how a body works.

clue.text: Increasingly mature bachelor's left more confident

indicators.note: bachelor's left means the bachelor has gone from the word

explanation.surface: A single man grows more self-assured with age.
explanation.definitionFit: Older means more advanced in age, more mature by degrees.

clue.text: Sweets are most pleasant in the centre

indicators.note: only the centre of the word is kept, losing first and last letters

explanation.surface: Sweets with the nicest soft middles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link. Ices, a British word, are ice creams or sorbets.
explanation.definitionFit: Ices are frozen desserts, a kind of sweet course.

clue.text: Lyric Roman Catholic backed for part of Mass

indicators.note: backed means the pieces are read in reverse order and direction

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: A Catholic choir piece supported for a section of the service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns the whole of ODE + RC round, giving CREDO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Credo, the Creed, is a sung or spoken section of the Mass.

clue.text: Devil worshipper is featured in stirring tabloid

indicators.note: featured in means placed inside the rearranged word
stirring the word tabloid mixes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A Satanist appears in a sensational newspaper story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stirring' turns TABLOID into DIABOLT, and 'featured in' puts IS inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A diabolist practises diabolism, the worship of the Devil.

clue.text: Anger when Irish nation is abandoned by English

indicators.note: abandoned by means the English letter leaves the word

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: Fury when the English leave Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ire is wrath, a literary word for anger.

clue.text: Letter-writing style succeeded — answer is stimulating that's sent back

parts.note: S abbreviates succeeded, as in family trees

indicators.note: sent back tells us to read the word for is stimulating in reverse

explanation.surface: A handwriting style worked, and the reply excites the person whose letter is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's sent back' reverses FIRES to SERIF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sans serif is a typeface style without small strokes at letter ends.

clue.text: Live where Elsie, Lacie and Tillie did, at the back of beyond?

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.words: where Elsie, Lacie and Tillie did
parts.note: in Alice in Wonderland the Dormouse tells of three sisters by these names who lived at the bottom of a well

explanation.surface: Asking where three little sisters lived, out in the middle of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The three girls lived in a treacle well in the Dormouse's story in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell is to live in or inhabit a place.
